newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai police kill four in two shootouts.
newsitem.headline: Thai police kill four in two shootouts.

text.p: Thai police said on Wednesday they had killed two suspected bank robbers and two suspected drug dealers in separate shootouts in less than 24 hours.

Police in northern Chiangrai town told Reuters they had killed the suspected robbers along a highway on Wednesday after the pair robbed a bank in the area and fled on a motorcycle with a large amount of cash.
In southern Nakorn Prathom province, police said they had killed two suspects said to be in possession of amphetamines in another shoot-out.
Some Thai politicians have alleged that the police force, in a campaign to stop the widespread abuse of amphetamines, may be using shoot-to-kill measures against offenders.
At least six suspects believed to be drug traffickers have been shot dead over the past two weeks, according to police reports.
Last November police shot dead six suspected amphetamine dealers in a single shooting incident.
The shooting sparked widespread criticism of the police by politicians and academics.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh defended the shooting of the six suspected traffickers and told foreign reporters on Tuesday that the police were only doing their job.
